title: In vivo organ specific drug delivery with implantable peristaltic pumps
protocol: Adhere to NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
Maintain Sprague Dawley male rats on a 12 h light 12 h dark schedule.
Feed rats with a normal salt diet (0.49% NaCl Teklad TD.96208) ad libitum.
Use proper aseptic technique for all animal surgeries.
Sterilize all drapes, supplies, surgery tools, and gloves before use.
Anesthetize rats with 2% isoflurane.
Give carprofen (5 mg/kg) and buprenorphine (0.1 mg/kg) subcutaneously to minimize pain post-surgery.
Shave hair just lateral to the left rib cage of the rat.
Prepare the skin by wiping alternately with 10% betadine and 70% ethanol.
Make a small incision through the skin and muscle to expose the kidney.
Carefully free the adrenal gland from the upper pole of the renal capsule.
Ligate the renal pedicle with 5-0 silk suture.
Remove the kidney after ligation.
Suture close the muscle with 4-0 prolene suture.
Close the skin incision with surgical staples.
Clean the area with 3% hydrogen peroxide in water.
Inject the incision site with a mixture of 0.25% Marcaine and 0.5% lidocaine (mixed 50/50).
Place the animal in a clean cage after surgery.
Allow the animal to recover for 7 days before iPRECIO® surgery.
Keep new iPRECIO® model smp-200 pumps in their sterile packaging.
Fill the pumps with sterile saline using a 27 gauge needle and syringe.
Pierce the needle through the packaging into the pump and fill with ~1 ml of saline to ensure catheter is also filled.
Program the pump using the iPRECIO® communication device and software.
Detect the pump in the communication device for the first time.
Program the pump settings accordingly.
Activate the pump after programming.
Place activated pumps in sterile saline within 50 ml tubes.
Incubate the pumps in a 37°C oven until surgery.
Remove the pumps from saline at the time of surgery.
Cut the catheter to a length of 6 cm.
Punch a 5 mm circle of Alliedsil™ with a one hole puncher.
Create a hole in the center of the Alliedsil™ circle using a 23 gauge needle.
Thread the iPRECIO® catheter through the Alliedsil™ circle using the needle.
Insert a small piece (1-2 cm) of micro medical grade catheter vinyl tubing V/1 into the catheter.
Glue the piece of vinyl tubing in place carefully, avoiding excess glue and ensuring it does not interfere with insertion into the kidney or close off the end of the catheter.
Remove any excess glue using cotton gauze if necessary.
Trim the tip of the V/1 tubing to 8 mm or adjust based on desired depth for kidney insertion.
Place the pump in warmed sterile saline containing 1% pen/strep until ready for implantation into the rat.
Anesthetize the rats with 2% isoflurane.
Give a subcutaneous injection of carprofen (5 mg/kg) and buprenorphine (0.1 mg/kg) to minimize pain.
Shave the area just below the ribs on the back side of the animal and disinfect it using alternating wipes of betadine and 70% ethanol.
Make an incision through the skin but not into muscle tissue, creating a large pocket between the muscle layer and the skin for accommodating the pump.
Insert the pump with the reservoir facing towards the head of the rat into the muscle using 4-0 prolene suture.
Make a small incision through the muscle to the peritoneum, exposing the kidney.
Hold the kidney away from the skin by propping it up with a sterile cotton swab.
Using a 23 gauge needle, make a small hole in the renal capsule where the catheter will be inserted, being careful to remain superficial to avoid damage to the kidney and excess bleeding.
Remove any blood from the area with a sterile cotton swab.
Apply drops of Vetbond™ tissue adhesive sparingly around the Alliedsil™ circle using a 27 gauge needle syringe.
Insert the catheter into the hole generated above.
Hold the catheter in place for 2 min while Vetbond dries, using forceps.
Gently return the kidney to its normal position within the body.
Suture the muscle wall to close it up.
Staple the skin closed over the pump area.
Place a mixture of 0.25% Marcaine and 0.5% lidocaine (mixed 50/50) on the incision site for pain relief.
Return the rats to clean cages and house them individually.
Anesthetize the rats with 2% isoflurane, placing them ventral side down (back up).
Shave the back of the rat where the pump resides to allow feeling the refill port with a gloved finger.
Disinfect the area around the refill port using alternating wipes of betadine and 70% ethanol.
Feel for the curved side of the refill port of the pump with your gloved finger.
Move your finger from the side to the top of the pump.
Stick a sterile 1 ml syringe with a 27-gauge needle where you feel the needle will hit the bottom of the refill port.
Place another gloved finger on the reservoir.
Feel if the reservoir is full or emptied.
Insert an empty, sterile 1 ml syringe with 27-gauge needle through the skin into the port to remove the current solution.
Withdraw the solution slowly while placing a gloved finger on the reservoir.
Insert a filled, sterile 1 ml syringe with 27-gauge needle through the skin to fill the pump.
Place another gloved finger on the reservoir as you dispense your volume (max 900 μl).
Feel the reservoir expand as it fills while dispensing the solution.
Clean the pumps of any obvious tissue or blood.
Fill the reservoir with sterile saline once cleaned.
Program the pump for an extra day to pump sterile saline through the catheter.
Keep the reservoir full with sterile saline after the pumps stop pumping.
Place the pumps in a beaker containing 7 g haemo-sol enzymatic cleaner per 500 ml of diH2O.
Soak the pumps for 72 hours at room temperature.
Wash pumps in sterile deionized water.
Place pumps in 2% glutaraldehyde for 12 h at room temperature.
Transfer pumps to sterile saline + 100 U/ml Penicillin + 100 μg/ml Streptomycin until next use.
When ready to reuse, place pumps in fresh sterile saline + 100 U/ml Penicillin + 100 μg/ml Streptomycin.
Refill pumps with fresh saline and go through programming steps again.
Once the pump is detected, programmed, and activated, return it to the saline + 100 U/ml Penicillin + 100 μg/ml Streptomycin.
Place the pump in a 37°C oven until surgery.
